clue.text: One who boasts of energy scam

parts.note: gas is fuel, a source of energy, and colloquially drive or pep
a con is a swindle or scam

explanation.surface: A braggart is exposed as the brains behind a fraud over power supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Gascons, natives of Gascony in France, were proverbial braggarts, hence 'gasconade' for boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gascony's people had a reputation for bragging, so the name came to mean any boaster.

clue.text: Satisfied when prepared for firing?

definitions.meaning: thankful and content with what one has been given
read as two words, a fireplace grate filled with fuel ready to be lit

explanation.definitionFit: Being thankful is a form of contentment; the second sense splits the word into a grate that is full.

clue.text: Chips are fried to look heavenly

indicators.note: frying cooks the chips so these letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Fried chips are so good they seem to come from heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fried' scrambles CHIPSARE into the answer; 'to look' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphs are the highest angels, so the adjective describes something angelic or celestial.

clue.text: Redhead involved in flower arrangement

indicators.note: being caught up inside means the head letter goes into the river's name

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Oder runs between Germany and Poland
the head, or first letter, of the word red

explanation.surface: A red-haired florist is busy putting together a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword trick for a river, here the ODER; 'involved in' puts R inside it after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting things in order is arranging them, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: One carrying offensive weapon, who refuses to strike a poet

parts.note: a scab is a worker who will not join a strike
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: An armed poet crosses a picket line, declining to join the walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: The offensive weapon is a sword, and the sheath carries it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath holds a sword or dagger, literally carrying the weapon at the wearer's side.

clue.text: Man's hair lacks style, producing great puzzlement

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Man's hair lacks style, producing great puzzlement (5,8)' is held with answer CHRISMASLANKA: an exact anagram of MANSHAIRLACKS, but not a recognised phrase meaning great puzzlement, so the definition cannot be explained honestly.
annotationWithheld.clue: Man's hair lacks style, producing great puzzlement

clue.text: Element used to a degree in ointment

indicators.note: attached to, so the element's name is joined on after the degree

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
silicon is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A chemist puts a pinch of some element into a soothing cream.
explanation.walkthrough: Basilicon is an old name for a resin-based salve.
explanation.definitionFit: Basilicon was a historical healing salve made from resin and wax, a kind of medicinal balm.

clue.text: Charm a cross model

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T stands for model

explanation.surface: A lucky charm is a scowling fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective for angry, but it is the hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm or talisman worn to ward off evil.

clue.text: Boy is given time to leave off

parts.note: Des, short for Desmond, is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad is told it's time to stop what he's doing.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or stop doing something, which is what leaving off means.

clue.text: Dog deprived of drink when put on show

indicators.note: having something taken away, so the drink's letters come out of the dog's name

parts.note: the Airedale is a breed of terrier
ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A dog is denied water while being exhibited at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ALE from the end of AIREDALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aired has been broadcast or displayed publicly.

clue.text: Frolics by cutpurse may be growing

parts.note: larks are pranks or frolics
the word purse cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A pickpocket's pranks may be going on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutpurse' looks like a thief but splits as 'cut purse', PURSE with its tail docked.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspurs are garden flowers, delphiniums, so they are things that may be growing in a bed.

clue.text: Cultured mole?

parts.note: a spy, or mole, of the bookish sort: someone who works with authors on behalf of publishers

explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a secret agent, and cultured suggests books, so the phrase describes an author's representative.

clue.text: Drunk hates pure running water

indicators.note: being drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunkard despises clean flowing water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a great river of Mesopotamia, flowing through Turkey, Syria and Iraq.

clue.text: Deposit not so much about nothing

indicators.note: surrounding, so the word for not so much goes round the zero

parts.note: less means a smaller amount
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A depositor puts in a smaller amount, close to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is a fine wind-blown silt laid down as a geological deposit.

clue.text: Little matter of amount prince dissipated

indicators.note: squandered and scattered, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: How much a prince wasted is of little concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Unimportance is the state of mattering little.

clue.text: Lords' clique?

parts.note: a gang of peers of the realm, punning on the everyday phrase for one's social equals

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means people of one's own age or status; here it is read as a set of noble lords.

clue.text: One is beset by cats, which can be dangerous

indicators.note: surrounded on all sides, so the big cats go round the other letters

parts.note: lions are big cats
a means one

explanation.surface: A lone person surrounded by cats is in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Les Liaisons dangereuses, the French novel of seduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Liaisons are affairs, which can be risky, as in the title of Laclos's novel.

clue.text: Refused licence for modified corn seed

indicators.note: genetically altered, so the letters are changed into another order

explanation.surface: A permit is denied for genetically modified seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A censored work has been denied permission for release, refused a licence.

clue.text: Possibly Rover part number covers force for propulsion

parts.note: Rover is a traditional dog's name, so possibly a pet
a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: goes over, so the number wraps round the letter for force

parts.note: nine is a number
g is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: A Rover car part number is listed under the heading of propulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover suggests the British car maker, but here it is a typical dog's name; 'covers' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A petrol engine drives a vehicle, so it is a machine for propulsion.

clue.text: Trollopean character's not on the level

definitions.meaning: the Reverend Obadiah Slope of Trollope's Barchester Towers, with a possessive

explanation.definitionFit: Mr Slope is the scheming chaplain in Trollope's novel; something that inclines is not level.

clue.text: Architectural feature erected in plain, if tasteful, fashion

indicators.note: in a down clue, set upright means read from the bottom up
the letters sit inside the words plain and if

explanation.surface: A building ornament is put up in a plain but tasteful style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run LAINIF inside 'plain, if', and 'erected' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A finial is an ornament crowning a gable, spire or post.

clue.text: Prone to deception?

explanation.definitionFit: Lying means both stretched out flat and telling falsehoods.

clue.text: A song about parasites, they say, but they're not certain

indicators.note: turned round, so the word for song is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: signals a homophone: the parasites' name is heard, not seen

parts.note: ticks are blood-sucking parasites, which sound like tics

explanation.surface: A ditty about bloodsuckers leaves its listeners in doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SONG into GNOS; 'they say' makes TICKS sound like TICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnostics hold that God's existence cannot be known, so they are uncertain.

clue.text: Capital of 1 in South Africa

indicators.note: placed inside, so the abbreviation for South Africa surrounds the letters

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A capital city lies within South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' looks like a cross-reference to 1 across but is just the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Nothing male about a boy first raped by Tereus

indicators.note: comes first, so the boy's name heads the answer

parts.note: Phil is a boy's name
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: turned about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: No man went near a boy who came first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges MALE to MELA. In Greek myth King Tereus raped Philomela, who was turned into a nightingale.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ovid's Metamorphoses Philomela is the sister-in-law whom Tereus raped and mutilated.

clue.text: As spelt perhaps, but its homonym would be a bloomer

indicators.note: a word sounding the same, so a flower's name is heard as the answer

parts.note: a bloomer is something that blooms, a flower

explanation.surface: A spelling mistake is described as a blooper.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelt is an ancient wheat ground for baking, not a past tense; a bloomer is also a British loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt is a grain milled into a baking powder, so it is an example of that pantry staple.

clue.text: Spy one felt resorted to maudlin emotion

indicators.note: sorted again, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spy who felt sorry for himself turned to sentimentality.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-pity is the indulgent, tearful feeling of being sorry for oneself.

clue.text: Took a break from habit in habitation

indicators.note: placed inside, so the word for home wraps round the custom

parts.note: a pad is slang for one's home
use is a habit or custom

explanation.surface: A monk took time off from his habit at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests a monk's robe, but it is USE, custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Pausing is stopping briefly, taking a short break.
